sn.s: En español uno no está con hambre.
sn.e: In Spanish you are not with hunger.
You have hunger.
I am hungry.
Roberto is hungry.

sn.s: Doña Carmen pregunta si tengo hambre.
sn.e: Doña Carmen asks if I am hungry.
She always asks if I am hungry.

sn.s: Y con este calor uno tiene sed.
sn.e: And in this heat you get thirsty.
I am thirsty all day.

sn.s: Tomo agua y tengo sed otra vez.
sn.e: I drink water and I am thirsty again.
In the afternoon I get sleepy.

sn.s: Todos tienen sueño a las dos.
sn.e: Everybody is sleepy at two.
This heat makes you sleepy.

sn.s: En la noche a veces tengo frío.
sn.e: At night sometimes I am cold.
Roberto does not understand that.
"Cold? Here?" the kid says.
For him it is never cold.
On the first day I was afraid.
I was afraid of the street.
I was afraid of speaking badly.
Now I am less afraid.
Doña Carmen is never in a hurry.
Nobody is in a hurry here.

sn.s: Yo tengo prisa y no sirve de nada.
sn.e: I am in a hurry and it does me no good.
The bus comes when it comes.
The water comes when it comes.

sn.s: Y tener prisa no cambia nada.
sn.e: And being in a hurry changes nothing.

sn.s: Un día le digo a Roberto que tengo prisa.
sn.e: One day I tell Roberto I am in a hurry.
"In a hurry for what?" he asks.
I do not know what to answer.
"You're right," I say to him.
And that is another one with tener.
You have reason - you are right.
Vos tenés razón.
Doña Carmen is always right.
That afternoon I am tired.
I walked a lot and I am tired.

sn.s: Me siento cansado y con sed.
sn.e: I feel tired and thirsty.

sn.s: Doña Carmen me ve la cara.
sn.e: Doña Carmen sees my face.
"How are you feeling, mijo?"
"Tired," I say. "And hungry."
"Then eat and sleep."
That is what I do.

sn.s: Como con hambre y duermo con sueño.
sn.e: I eat hungry and I sleep sleepy.

sn.s: En la noche me siento mejor.
sn.e: At night I feel better.

sn.s: Aprendo que el cuerpo se dice con tener.
sn.e: I learn that the body is said with tener.

sn.s: Tengo hambre. Tengo sed. Tengo sueño.
sn.e: I am hungry. I am thirsty. I am sleepy.

sn.s: Tengo frío. Tengo miedo. Tengo prisa.
sn.e: I am cold. I am afraid. I am in a hurry.
And I am right, sometimes.
But you are tired.
Tiredness goes with estar.
Nobody explains why to me.
Roberto does not know why.
"That is how you say it," he says.
And that is how you say it.
